stack_summary: React.js + Vite + Tailwind CSS frontend · Node.js + Express REST API · MySQL 8 (primary) + PostgreSQL (notifications) · Elasticsearch (search/autocomplete) · JWT + bcrypt auth · RBAC in-app admin

categories.name: Project Structure & Naming
rules: Name React component files and component functions in PascalCase (e.g. ProductCard.jsx); all other JS/TS files in camelCase; directories and non-component assets in kebab-case.
Organise the frontend as: src/components/, src/pages/, src/hooks/, src/services/, src/store/, src/utils/, src/tokens/; no logic outside these top-level folders.
Organise the backend as: src/routes/, src/controllers/, src/services/, src/models/, src/middleware/, src/config/; every HTTP route delegates to a controller, every controller delegates to a service.
Export exactly one component per file; co-locate its CSS module or Tailwind variants in the same directory only if component-scoped styles are needed.

categories.name: Components & UI
rules: Write all React components as named arrow-function components with explicit prop destructuring; no class components.

Consume all design values (colour, spacing, typography, border-radius) exclusively from Tailwind design tokens defined in tailwind.config.js — never hard-code hex values, px numbers, or rem literals inline.
Use Tailwind utility classes directly in JSX; never write raw CSS or inline style objects except for programmatically computed values that cannot be expressed as tokens.

Every interactive element (button, input, link, select) must have an accessible label (aria-label, aria-labelledby, or visible <label>); colour contrast must meet WCAG AA (4.5:1 text, 3:1 large text).
All keyboard-navigable flows (browse → PDP → cart → checkout) must be operable with Tab/Enter/Escape and include visible focus rings — never suppress outline without a replacement.
Use React.lazy + Suspense for route-level code splitting on all page components; never import page components eagerly in the router.
Poll the notification REST endpoint with a fixed interval using a custom useNotifications hook; never open a WebSocket or SSE connection for notifications in this release.

categories.name: State, Data Fetching & Routing
rules: Use React Query (TanStack Query) for all server-state fetching, caching, and mutations; never store fetched server data in useState or Redux.
Reserve Zustand (or React Context) for client-only global state (cart, auth session, UI flags); keep stores small and single-responsibility.
Define all API base URLs, polling intervals, and environment flags in .env files accessed only via a central src/config/env.js — never reference import.meta.env directly in components.
Use React Router v6 <Routes> with route-level auth guards implemented as wrapper components checking JWT claims; never duplicate RBAC checks inside individual components.

categories.name: API & Backend
rules: Every Express route file registers only route definitions; all business logic lives in the corresponding service file; controllers handle request/response mapping only.
Use parameterised queries via mysql2 prepared statements or an ORM query-builder for every MySQL query — never concatenate user input into SQL strings.
Use the pg parameterised query interface for every PostgreSQL (notifications) query — same rule as MySQL.
All Elasticsearch queries must be built as structured query DSL objects — never interpolate user input into query strings.

Expose a single PaymentService interface (charge, refund, getStatus) that wraps the mock provider; swap the implementation via dependency injection through config — no payment-provider SDK calls outside this service.
Never log, store, or transmit raw card data anywhere in the codebase; the payment service accepts only tokenised references.
Apply rate-limiting middleware (express-rate-limit) specifically to POST /auth/login and POST /auth/password-reset before any other middleware on those routes.
Authenticate all protected routes with a validateJwt middleware that verifies signature and expiry; authorise staff/admin routes with a requireRole(roleName) middleware applied at the router level.
Password-reset tokens must be stored hashed, tied to an expiry timestamp, and invalidated immediately after first use.
Hash all passwords with bcrypt at a minimum cost factor of 12 before persistence; never store or log the plaintext password at any point.

categories.name: Error Handling, Logging & Security
rules: All Express errors must flow to a single global error-handling middleware (err, req, res, next) that maps domain errors to HTTP status codes and returns a consistent JSON envelope { success, error: { code, message } }.
Use a structured logger (pino) for all server-side logging; log at info/warn/error levels with a request-id field — never use console.log in production code paths.
Never log JWT secrets, passwords, raw card data, or PII (email, phone) at any log level.
Set HTTP security headers via helmet on every Express response; enable CORS only for the configured frontend origin.
JWT access tokens must include role claims, be short-lived (≤15 min), and be refreshed via a separate httpOnly-cookie refresh-token endpoint.

categories.name: Business Logic & Calculations
rules: Perform all monetary arithmetic (GST, discounts, free-shipping threshold) in integer paise on the server; never use floating-point for currency calculations.
Apply the free-shipping waiver (orders ≥ ₹799) and GST calculation exclusively inside the OrderService — never in the frontend or controller layer.
Enforce SKU-level stock checks atomically inside a MySQL transaction before confirming any order; never confirm an order without a successful payment callback.
